newsitem.title: USA: Innovex expects FY97 EPS to top estimates.
newsitem.headline: Innovex expects FY97 EPS to top estimates.

text.p: Innovex Inc said Tuesday it expects earnings for its fiscal year ending September 30, 1997 to exceed analysts' mean estimate of $1.51 a share.

"I expect our first quarter to be our 'low' quarter," Innovex Chairman and Chief Executive Thomas Haley told Reuters. "We see sequential increases in earnings per share for the year. If you take $0.42 (EPS in Q1) and multiply it by four, you get $1.62."
"I think we'll do a little better than that because we'll have those sequential improvements in earnings" Haley said in an interview before Innovex's annual meeting in Minneapolis.
According to a survey of analysts by First Call, the mean estimate for Innovex's earnings for fiscal year 1997 ended September 30 was $1.51 a share.
Innovex posted earnings of $0.93 a share in fiscal 1996.
Haley added that the company's lead wire assembly production capacity would increase by 20 percent by April.

"We're pretty much at capacity now with production of (lead wire assemblies) slightly above 10 million per week," he said. "We'll have about a 20-percent increase in capacity by the end of April, so we'll have five months of that capacity in fiscal year 1997."
Haley said the company's shipments of its wire alignment tab (WAT) product may increase from current levels of one million per week to two million by the end of the fiscal year.

"We're committed to our primary customer and we have two customers who are very interested in our WAT product," he explained. "Though they haven't got the orders yet we told them we'd be able to commit to production in the April-May time frame. My guess is we'll be shipping two million WAT product per week by the end of the (fiscal) year."
WAT is a positioning device that allows the lead wire to be more easily attached to disk drives in microcomputers.
On another front, Haley said the company expects its InnoMedica division to be "in the black" by the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997. The division lost $1.8 million in fiscal 1996.
Haley also said the company's Iconovex software development division may be up for sale by this summer.
"We have put June as the benchmark for finding a marketing partner and if we're not successful at that, we'll start looking for a buyer," he said.
Innovex develops specialty electromagnetic products, chemically engineered components and indexing software.
